# The isoformic method

`isoformic` interprets RNA-seq data at the level of annotated transcripts.
Instead of asking only whether a gene changes between conditions, it asks which of its isoforms change, what type of transcript they are (protein coding, retained intron, nonsense-mediated decay, ...) and how the expression of the gene is distributed across them.

Everything revolves around the `IsoformicExperiment` object.
It holds, for the same samples, transcript-level assays, gene-level assays derived from them, the exon structures of every annotated transcript and the differential expression results, all backed by Parquet files on disk.

This article builds the object from quantification and differential expression tables and shows how to look at it.
The analyses have one article each:

- [Transcriptomic diversity](isoformic-diversity.html): how many isoforms a gene uses, which one dominates and where isoform switches happen.
- [Quantification uncertainty](isoformic-uncertainty.html): how well the reads determine each isoform, which isoforms cannot be told apart and how confident each differential expression call is.
- [What makes an isoform hard to quantify?](isoformic-quantification-stability.html): which isoforms the reads leave uncertain, why, and how many Gibbs draws are enough.
- [Isoform structure and productivity](isoformic-productivity.html): open reading frames, nonsense-mediated decay, productive fractions, poison exons and external evidence.
- [Alternative polyadenylation](isoformic-polyadenylation.html): 3' end usage and 3' UTR length.
- [Functional enrichment by transcript type](isoformic-enrichment.html): gene set enrichment run separately for coding and unproductive transcripts.
- [Plots](isoformic-plots.html): fold-change, expression profile and genomic context plots.
- [Other annotations](isoformic-references.html): T2T-CHM13, Ensembl, RefSeq, haplotype-resolved assemblies, FANTOM CAT and long-read catalogs.
- [Working with plain tables](isoformic-tables.html): the table-based counterparts of every step.

To start from Salmon output instead of ready-made tables, see [From Salmon quantifications to an IsoformicExperiment](isoformic-preprocess.html).

## The data

The examples use the placenta RNA-seq dataset from ["Landscape of Dysregulated Placental RNA Editing Associated With Preeclampsia"][pe-paper-ref]: 8 preeclamptic and 17 control placentas quantified with Salmon [@salmon] against GENCODE v33 and tested for differential expression at the transcript level with `swish` [@swish] and at the gene level with `DESeq2`.
The tables ship with the package as Parquet files.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(isoformic)
library(dplyr)

extdata <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata")
fs::dir_ls(extdata)
```

```{r}
abundance <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_abundance.parquet"))
col_data <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_col_data.parquet"))
det <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_det.parquet"))
deg <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_deg.parquet"))

abundance[1:3, 1:4]
col_data
head(det)
head(deg)
```

## The annotation

`isoformic` relies on the transcript types of the [GENCODE][gencode-ref] annotation.
The annotation must be the one used for quantification, here GENCODE v33.
`download_reference()` fetches it into the package cache (this step needs an internet connection the first time) and `prepare_isoformic_annotation()` converts the GFF3 file, once, into a directory of Parquet tables.

```{r}
gff_file <- download_reference(version = "33", file_type = "gff")
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(gff_file)
fs::dir_ls(annot_dir)
```

The tables can be inspected with `read_parquet()`, but normally the object reads them for you.

```{r}
read_parquet(fs::path(annot_dir, "annot_data_transcripts.parquet"), n_max = 3)
```

The cache location and every other setting the package reads are documented in `?isoformic-options`.

## Building the IsoformicExperiment

A transcript-level abundance table (TPM) with the sample metadata is all that is needed.
Transcript IDs are checked against the annotation, sample IDs against the metadata.

```{r}
iso <- IsoformicExperiment(
  experiment_name = "preeclampsia_placenta",
  annot_path = annot_dir,
  assays = list(abundance = abundance),
  col_data = col_data
)
iso
```

The object behaves like a `SummarizedExperiment`:

```{r}
dim(iso)
assay(iso, "abundance")[1:3, 1:3]
head(row_data(iso))
col_data(iso)
iso[1:5, 1:3]
```

Gene-level assays are derived on demand by summing the isoforms of each gene and cached.

```{r}
gene_assay(iso, "abundance")[1:3, 1:3]
head(gene_data(iso))
```

## Adding differential expression results

Results from any tool can be attached: column names such as `log2FoldChange`, `padj`, `logFC` or `FDR` are standardised to `log2FC`, `pvalue` and `qvalue`, and IDs are validated against the annotation.
Significance is flagged with stored cutoffs (absolute log2 fold-change of 1 and adjusted p-value of 0.05 by default).

```{r}
de_tx(iso) <- det
de_gene(iso) <- deg
de_cutoffs(iso)

head(de_tx(iso, sig_only = TRUE))
head(de_gene(iso, sig_only = TRUE))
```

`de_table()` combines both levels in one long table, one row per feature, which is what the plots consume.

```{r}
de_table(iso) |>
  filter(gene_name == "RBPJ")
```

## A first look

The fold-change plot compares the change of a gene with that of each of its transcripts, coloured by transcript type; the [plots article](isoformic-plots.html) covers the others.

```{r}
plot_log2fc(iso, feature = "RBPJ")
```

## Saving the experiment

The whole object, including results, is written as a directory of Parquet files and restored with `read_isoformic()`.

```{r}
out_dir <- fs::path(tempdir(), "preeclampsia_placenta")
iso <- write_isoformic(iso, out_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
iso@data_path
fs::dir_ls(out_dir, recurse = TRUE)
read_isoformic(out_dir)
```

Every other article starts from this object; the block below is all it takes to rebuild it.

```{r}
#| eval: false
library(isoformic)
extdata <- fs::path_package("isoformic", "extdata")
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(download_reference(version = "33", file_type = "gff"))
iso <- IsoformicExperiment(
  experiment_name = "preeclampsia_placenta",
  annot_path = annot_dir,
  assays = list(abundance = read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_abundance.parquet"))),
  col_data = read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_col_data.parquet"))
)
de_tx(iso) <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_det.parquet"))
de_gene(iso) <- read_parquet(fs::path(extdata, "pe_deg.parquet"))
```

## Citing isoformic

If you use `isoformic` in publications, please cite @isoformic; `citation("isoformic")` prints the reference.
